title: HMRC's Connect data-matching system: about £4.6 billion of additional yield in 2024-25, per HMRC FOI response
summary: HMRC's Connect data-matching system yielded ~£4.6bn extra tax in 2024-25 per FOI; C&AG confirms its use to stop risky repayments
account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010-11, describing it in its annual report as an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data from across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated on average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield, about £4.6 billion in 2024-25, with around 4,300 staff using the system. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024-25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment) to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation, replaced by IDRS from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.
purpose: Match and analyze data from many sources to identify tax non-compliance and risky repayment claims
system: HMRC Connect (data-matching and risk analytics) and TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment)
domain: Tax administration: compliance and fraud detection
taxonomy_note: Closest fit; the benefit is additional compliance yield for the Exchequer. Whether Connect counts as AI is contested: official documents call it data analytics and risk rules.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: aggregate yield with no discrete attributable event.
General benefit without an event: the £4.6 billion figure is HMRC's own annual attribution via FOI, not an audited event.
General benefit without an event: aggregate national revenue figure.

ai_role.statement: Yield attribution to Connect comes from HMRC's FOI response as reported by Pinsent Masons; no independent evaluation apportions yield between the system and caseworkers. The NAO's audit report describes TRUCE/IDRS as automated risk-assessment of repayment claims whose controls it reviewed, without quantifying stopped repayments. The cited sources describe the system as data analytics and risk rules rather than machine learning.
